subject: Re: Performance & concurrency follow-up — Acme (latency SLOs, rate limits)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Soto <jenna.soto@acme.com>, Rahul Patel <rahul.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + concurrency / SLO questions

Thanks again for the call today — great to hear more about the chat experience you're building. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on performance/SLO asks and what Redwood can provision for the proof-of-concept (POC):

TL;DR (ask): please confirm the concurrency profile below and whether the Streaming/partial-token behavior is required for all endpoints. Once you confirm we can provision a temporary quota bump for the POC (30 days) and share an updated SOW.

What you described (please confirm):
- Primary use-case: customer support chat with live typing and streaming tokens to UI.
- P95 latency target (server-side, end-to-end token emission): <= 300ms for messages up to ~300 token responses.
- Typical request characteristics: median input + output ~350 tokens; peaks up to 1k tokens.
- Sustained throughput: ~1,500 requests / minute (25 rps) across global users.
- Concurrency: estimated peak concurrent requests = 120 (concurrent in-flight streams), typical steady = ~60.
- Connection pattern: many clients behind a small pool of frontend servers; plan to use HTTP keep-alive + connection pooling (one pool per frontend host).

Redwood asks / constraints we raised on the call:
- We have per-account rate limits and concurrency quotas by default. For Hosted customers these are conservative; for Dedicated/Enterprise we can configure higher reserved concurrency and token-rate quotas.
- Streaming increments token accounting as tokens are emitted; it affects token-rate quotas rather than only request-rate quotas.

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
1) You confirm the numbers above (peak vs steady concurrency, streaming requirements).
2) We will provision a 30-day elevated quota for the POC: reserved concurrency = 250, request-rate cap = 2,000 rps burst 2,500 for 1-minute windows, token-rate limit to support ~1.2M tokens/min (covers peaks).
3) We will share a short SOW + draft MPA and a technical runbook (how to tune pooling, keep-alive, and batching) — attaching the concurrency proposal.
4) Technical call with Vivek tomorrow to validate connection pooling and streaming behavior against your frontend.

Attachments: redwood-concurrency-proposal.pdf (application/pdf, 48KB)

Open questions for you:
- Is the 120 concurrent streams peak per region or global?
- Are all clients required to receive partial-streamed tokens, or can some endpoints use non-streaming responses?
- What is your procurement timeline (SLA/MPA signoff target)?

Thanks — I can loop in Neha for procurement and Rishi for contract/discount questions once we have POC numbers.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Jenna Soto <jenna.soto@acme.com>

Cc: Rahul Patel <rahul.patel@acme.com>, Tom Mills <tom.mills@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 19:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + concurrency / SLO questions

Thanks Marissa — quick answers inline:  

- Peak concurrency: 120 is global peak across our US region (we expect EU to be significantly lower for the first phase).
- Streaming: yes, we need streaming for the agent UI so partial tokens should be emitted; we do have a couple of batch endpoints that can be non-streaming.
- Procurement: target signoff for POC by end of August; production MPA + reserved capacity decision by end of Q3.

Also: typical steady concurrency per frontend host is ~12–15, we have 8 frontend hosts for redundancy which explains the global 120 peak. Hope that helps.

Can you confirm whether Redwood wants per-client connection pools at that scale or if we should increase pool size on the frontends? We'll set up the technical call with Vivek tomorrow morning.

— Jenna
Jenna Soto | Dir, Product — Conversational Experience, Acme Industries
jenna.soto@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-0147

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Soto <jenna.soto@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + concurrency / SLO questions (technical notes)

Thanks — quick technical notes from my side ahead of the call:

1) Connection pooling guidance
- Use long-lived HTTP/1.1 keep-alive or HTTP/2 multiplexing from frontends to Redwood gateways. For your topology (8 frontends, steady ~12–15 per host) we recommend a pool of ~100 persistent connections per frontend host to avoid TCP churn during peaks.
- If using HTTP/2, multiplexing can reduce the total open connection count; ensure your load balancer doesn't terminate HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 which would block multiplexing benefits.

2) Mapping your requirements to Redwood quotas (what we'll provision for POC)
- Reserved concurrency (in-flight requests capable of streaming) = 250 (headroom above your 120 peak).
- Request-rate cap (global) = 2,000 requests/sec with burst to 2,500 for short 1–2 minute windows.
- Token-rate quota = configured to support ~1.2M tokens/min (covers typical + peaks for 1k-token responses).
- Per-client connection limits: no hard limit per individual client; we reason in terms of overall concurrency and connection pools per frontend.

3) Streaming considerations
- Streaming increments token accounting as tokens are emitted; for SLOs we measure server-side end-to-end emission latency and recommend instrumenting a small synthetic load that mirrors your median+tail token sizes.
- For low p95 (<300ms) we will pin models onto low-latency hardware and warm KV caches during the POC runs. This helps keep cold-start risk low.

4) Trial/quota mechanics
- We can open an elevated quota window for 30 days for the POC (no immediate contract needed) to validate latency and concurrency. After the trial, we convert to Reserved Capacity (monthly commit) with SLA.

I'll send a short technical runbook and the proposed quota numbers as an attached PDF. If that looks good we'll schedule the ramp test: 1) warmup, 2) steady-state, 3) peak stress (simulate 120 concurrent streaming sessions for 10 minutes).

Attachment: redwood-concurrency-proposal.pdf (application/pdf, 48KB)

— Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
